open_points.subject: agent identity on token-list re-read
open_points.text: “names are unique in an installation, and a configuration repeating one is refused at start” versus “Exactly three checks apply to a re-read: the file can be read and parsed; every token is at least 43 characters; no two tokens are equal.”
open_points.question: When the live token-list re-read introduces two agents with the same name but different tokens, must the re-read fail, or may both tokens produce the same Actor identity?
options: Reject the re-read for duplicate agent names
Accept duplicate names after start
Assign an additional stable identity not currently specified
open_points.default_guess: Reject the re-read for duplicate agent names.

open_points.subject: installation credential-header validation
open_points.text: “a header name — an HTTP field-name token, or the kernel refuses to start” but `installation.load_installation` enforces only file and token checks, while `bindings.check_installed_instances` enforces only header-name collisions.
open_points.question: Which start operation validates that every configured credential header name is an HTTP field-name token, and where does that check fall in start-error order?
options: `installation.load_installation` validates it
`bindings.check_installed_instances` validates it
No start validation; resolution fails later
open_points.default_guess: Validate it in `installation.load_installation` before installed-instance checks.

open_points.subject: configured service identifiers
open_points.text: “A `service_id` is one or more lowercase letters, digits and `_` only; any other is refused before a path is built” but no State 5 installation or start operation validates service identifiers used by configured credentials and selected instances.
open_points.question: Must configured service identifiers be validated before `bindings.check_installed_instances` constructs manifest paths, and which operation owns that refusal?
options: Validate all configured service IDs in `installation.load_installation`
Validate each ID in `bindings.check_installed_instances` before building a path
Apply the restriction only to binding proposals
open_points.default_guess: Validate all configured service IDs in `installation.load_installation`.

open_points.subject: manifest source at a revision
open_points.text: “reads a service's record only from `<manifest_location>/<service_id>.json` at the configured `manifest_revision`” and `installation.manifest_source` returns “the manifest location and revision fixed at start.”
open_points.question: What operation resolves `manifest_location` and `manifest_revision` to immutable bytes, including what kind of location and revision they are and whether working-tree changes at the same revision are visible?
options: Read the file blob directly from a Git revision
Treat the location as an already materialized immutable revision directory
Read the live filesystem and use the revision only as metadata
open_points.default_guess: Treat the location as a Git repository and read the file blob from the exact configured revision.

open_points.subject: binding and flow port schemas
open_points.text: Contracts require that “every `value_schema` is within the supported schema subset”; binding proposal checks mention only selected contract-port rules, and `flows.compose_flow_version` lists no corresponding schema-subset check for flow ports or constant-declared schemas.
open_points.question: Which ports and constant schemas must be in the supported schema subset, and does an unsupported schema cause proposal/composition refusal or a proof failure?
options: Validate every contract, binding, flow and constant schema when authored or proposed
Validate binding schemas on proposal and flow/constant schemas during proof
Only contract schemas are restricted
open_points.default_guess: Validate every declared port or constant schema at its authoring/proposal operation, before storing the record.

open_points.subject: schema stored for `many` values
open_points.text: “A value on a `many` port is a JSON array whose every element fits the port's `value_schema`” and mapped output lists use “the array schema with the port's schema as `items`,” but no rule fixes the StoredValue `value_schema` for other `many` values such as flow inputs, trial inputs, expected outputs, constants and service outputs.
open_points.question: Does a StoredValue containing a `many` value store the port's element schema or a synthesized array schema, and must that rule apply in every producer?
options: Always store a synthesized array schema with the port schema as `items`
Always store the port's element schema
Use the synthesized schema only for mapped outputs
open_points.default_guess: Always store the synthesized array schema for a `many` StoredValue.

open_points.subject: path-placeholder ports
open_points.text: Proposal accepts a placeholder when its input port's schema type is `string` or `integer`, while sending requires its value to be “a non-null string or integer”; neither proposal rule requires `carriage: value` or `cardinality: one`.
open_points.question: Are file-carriage or `many` ports with string/integer schemas valid path placeholders, and if not, must the binding be refused at proposal rather than every send ending `input_not_placeable`?
options: Require a `value`, `one` port at proposal
Allow them at proposal and fail placement at send
Allow `many` and define a path encoding for it
open_points.default_guess: Require a `value` port of cardinality `one` at proposal.

open_points.subject: service base URL
open_points.text: An instance address need only be “an absolute `http` or `https` URL with a host,” and the request URL is that value “without a trailing `/` followed by the declared path.”
open_points.question: May `api_base_url` contain user information, a non-root path, query, fragment, percent escapes or an IPv6 zone identifier, and exactly how are those components combined with the operation path and used for the `host` header?
options: Allow only scheme, host and optional port
Allow a base path but forbid user information, query and fragment
Allow every absolute URL and define component-wise resolution
open_points.default_guess: Allow only scheme, host and optional port.

open_points.subject: JSON request `Content-Type`
open_points.text: The headers sent include “with a body, `content-type` and `content-length`,” while only multipart bodies are given an exact content type; no value is specified for a non-multipart JSON body.
open_points.question: What exact `Content-Type` header value is sent for POST, PUT or PATCH JSON bodies and therefore included in the approval request description?
options: `application/json`
`application/json; charset=utf-8`
A release-defined value

open_points.subject: HTTP header value encoding
open_points.text: Required-header values are accepted unless empty, surrounded by whitespace or containing a control character and are sent “verbatim”; credential values are rejected only when empty or containing a control character.
open_points.question: Which character repertoire and byte encoding are allowed for required-header and credential values, and what happens to non-ASCII or leading/trailing-whitespace credential values that an HTTP library cannot send verbatim?
options: Require visible ASCII and reject anything else
Permit ISO-8859-1 bytes with a fixed mapping
Permit UTF-8 bytes in field values
open_points.default_guess: Require visible ASCII; classify invalid required headers as `required_header_invalid` and invalid credential values as `credential_unresolved`.

open_points.subject: service error `failure_detail`
open_points.text: “The body of an error response is not interpreted; at most `failure_detail_bytes_max` of it is kept as `failure_detail`” versus “A credential ... never enters ... a failure detail.”
open_points.question: How must `send_prepared_request` encode arbitrary response bytes and guarantee that a service which echoes the credential cannot place it in `failure_detail`?
options: Never retain service error bodies
Redact exact credential bytes before producing UTF-8 detail
Retain only bodies proven to be valid UTF-8 and not containing the credential
open_points.default_guess: Do not retain service error bodies; retain only non-body transport/status diagnostics.

open_points.subject: owner access to trial file fixtures
open_points.text: “The owner receives every value” versus “a file — StoredValue fixture or SpooledFile — as digest, size and media type, its bytes only through `read_spooled_file`,” while `read_spooled_file` takes “only a SpooledFile — never a StoredValue.”
open_points.question: Can the owner inspect the bytes of a trial-case file fixture, and if so through which public operation and with what inputs and output limit?
options: Extend `read_spooled_file` to accept file-carriage StoredValues
Add a separate fixture-byte inspection operation
The owner receives fixture metadata only despite the earlier rule
open_points.default_guess: Allow the owner to read a file-carriage StoredValue through a generalized byte-read inspection operation.

open_points.subject: standing grants for draft-write resends
open_points.text: `effects.grant_standing_approval` says “Later sends of that node in runs of that version need no approval,” but A10 says a resend after `not_applied` needs a fresh approval “whatever grant exists,” including `draft-write`.
open_points.question: Is the grant operation's observable-effect statement subject to the `not_applied` resend exception for every effect class?
options: Yes, every resend after `not_applied` needs fresh approval
No, a grant covers such resends
Only non-draft effects need fresh approval
open_points.default_guess: Yes; follow A10 and require a fresh approval for every resend after `not_applied`.

open_points.subject: rollback target ordering
open_points.text: Rollback is described as activating “an earlier implementation,” while its operative check only requires “an implementation of the slot's current contract version that already holds an `admitted` verdict over the current corpus.”
open_points.question: May rollback activate any qualifying non-current implementation, including one activated later than the current implementation, or only an implementation earlier in submission or activation order?
options: Any qualifying implementation
Only one submitted earlier than the current implementation
Only one whose latest activation precedes the current activation
open_points.default_guess: Allow any qualifying implementation, because the explicit eligibility rule imposes no temporal check.

open_points.subject: filtered pagination after lifecycle changes
open_points.text: A continuation token is “the store position of the last item returned” and is refused when it “names no position of that list”; statuses used as filters can change in place while keeping their original store positions.
open_points.question: If the cursor record changes status and no longer matches the filter between pages, does the token remain valid, and are later pages a live view or a snapshot of membership at the first page?
options: The absolute store-position cursor remains valid and each page uses current membership below it
The token becomes invalid when its record leaves the filtered list
The token captures snapshot membership for all pages
open_points.default_guess: Keep the absolute cursor valid and evaluate current membership only below that position.

open_points.subject: refusal reason length
open_points.text: State 5 says “A refusal's reason is at most `bounded_text_bytes_max`, cut at a UTF-8 character boundary,” while A20 says over-ceiling outputs are never truncated and “The one exception is `failure_detail`.”
open_points.question: May refusal reasons be truncated, or must every reason be constructed within the ceiling without truncation?
options: Construct every refusal reason within the ceiling
Permit truncation as a second explicit exception
Return only a fixed reason code when the full reason is too long
open_points.default_guess: Construct bounded refusal reasons without truncation.
